message.content:
**Average Apartment Rental Prices – New York City (FY 2025)**  

| Borough / Neighborhood | Median Monthly Rent* |
|------------------------|----------------------|
| Manhattan (Mid‑town)   | $4,200–$5,800        |
| Brooklyn (Williamsburg)| $2,900–$4,300        |
| Queens (Astoria)       | $1,950–$3,100        |
| Bronx (Riverdale)      | $1,650–$2,700        |
| Staten Island          | $1,400–$2,500        |

\*Median monthly rent for one‑bedroom apartments (prices vary widely depending on exact address, building age, floor level, view, and amenities).

### What Influences These Numbers?

| Factor | Typical Impact |
|-------|---------------|
| **Size** | A studio may start around $1,600 NYC‑wide; two‑bedrooms often range from $2,000 up to $7,000+ in prime locations. |
| **Borough & Neighborhood** | Manhattan remains the most expensive; outer boroughs offer more affordable options. Gentrifying areas (e.g., Bushwick, Long Island City) have seen rapid increases. |
| **Building Age & Amenities** | Newly built luxury high-rises with doormen, gyms, rooftop decks command premium rates—often 20% higher than older buildings without those perks. |
| **Floor Level & View** | Higher floors with skyline views typically add $150–$350/month over comparable units below. |
| **Lease Terms** | Shorter leases (≤12 months) sometimes carry a “premium” fee (~10%) compared to longer commitments. |
| **Utilities Included** | Some landlords include water, trash, or even internet; this can shift net rent upward if utilities were previously paid separately. |

### Quick Reference Ranges (by Unit Type)

| Unit Size | Average Range (NYC‑Wide) |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| Studio    | $1,550 – $2,250           |
| One‑Bedroom | $2,050 – $3,750         |
| Two‑Bedroom | $2,850 – $5,450         |
| Three‑Bedroom | $3,650 – $8,200       |

> *These figures reflect market averages reported by major real‑estate aggregators (Zillow, StreetEasy, RentCafe) through Q3 2025.*

---

#### How to Find Current Listings

1. **Online Marketplaces:**  
   - [StreetEasy](https://streeteasy.com/) – filters by neighborhood, unit size, lease length.  
   - [RentHop](https://www.renthop.com/) – includes “price alerts.”  
   - [Apartments.com](https://apartments.com/) – offers “average rent heat maps.”

2. **Brokerage Services:**  
   - Many brokers charge a flat commission (≈ one month’s rent), so factor that into your budget when negotiating.

3. **Local Newspapers & Community Boards:**  
   - For sublets or short-term rentals, check community Facebook groups or Craigslist under “For Rent – NYS”.

---

#### Tips If You’re Looking To Save Money

- **Consider Outer Boroughs:** Even within the same city, moving just outside Manhattan can reduce rent by ~30%.  
- **Look at Older Buildings:** Units above ground-floor levels in pre‑1970 structures tend to be cheaper.  
- **Negotiate Lease Length:** Landlords might lower the rate slightly for a year‑long commitment versus a six‑month lease.  
- **Share With Roommates:** Splitting a larger unit reduces individual cost dramatically.

Feel free to let me know which specific area you’re interested in, and I can drill down further!
